command: manually curated from this pass's code audit; verified by tests
note: Only defects actually reproduced and fixed (or explicitly accepted) are listed. Severity uses CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW. No credential values appear here.

defects.title: Client-supplied X-Forwarded-For was accepted as proof of loopback locality, bypassing mutation authorization
defects.introducedIn: pre-existing (present at df52c08 and all earlier commits)
defects.reproduction: With OMNI_API_TOKEN unset, authorizeMutation() on a request carrying only 'X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1' returned null (allowed) because clientIp() read the client-controlled first hop and isLoopbackOrPrivate() trusted it.
defects.impact: Any network client able to reach the API could assert locality and mutate engine, order, config and vault state without a token, whenever OMNI_API_TOKEN was not configured.
defects.fix: Forwarded headers no longer establish locality. isTrustedLocalClient() trusts a request only when it carries no forwarding headers (a direct connection) or when OMNI_TRUST_PROXY is enabled and the NEAREST hop (the last entry, appended by the proxy) is private. clientIp() reads the last hop only when the proxy is trusted.
regressionTests: scripts/run_comprehensive_tests.js — 'API Guard: a direct connection is treated as local, a forwarded one is not'
scripts/run_comprehensive_tests.js — 'API Guard: forwarded headers are honoured only when OMNI_TRUST_PROXY is set'
scripts/run_comprehensive_tests.js — webhook test corrected to reject spoofed XFF
scripts/audit_safety.js — SAFE-15
scripts/audit_safety.js — SAFE-09 corrected to assert a direct local connection
defects.verification: PASS — spoofed header rejected, direct connection allowed, client-prepended loopback rejected, trusted-proxy nearest hop allowed.

defects.title: Same-origin check was accepted as authentication for remote mutations
defects.reproduction: With OMNI_API_TOKEN unset, a non-browser client sending Host, Origin and X-Forwarded-For consistently passed originMatchesHost() and was allowed to mutate state. A test asserted this so the limitation could not be forgotten.
defects.impact: Any remote client that could set two request headers could mutate engine, order, config and vault state without a token.
defects.fix: originMatchesHost() no longer authorises a mutation. authorizeMutation() now permits a token-less mutation only from a genuinely local client; anything arriving through a proxy is rejected 401 AUTH_REQUIRED_FOR_REMOTE. Remote deployments must configure OMNI_API_TOKEN.
regressionTests: scripts/run_comprehensive_tests.js — 'API Guard: SEC-008 closed - a forgeable same-origin header does not authorise a remote mutation'
scripts/run_comprehensive_tests.js — 'API Guard: adversarial X-Forwarded-For handling (multi-hop, malformed, trusted proxy)'
scripts/run_comprehensive_tests.js — 'API Guard: every mutating API route is guarded'
scripts/audit_safety.js — SAFE-16
defects.verification: PASS — remote same-origin mutation rejected 401; same request with a bearer token allowed; local direct connection still allowed.

defects.title: Empty or whitespace-only X-Forwarded-For was read as a direct local connection
defects.introducedIn: pre-existing within this pass's SEC-007 fix (present in commit 90fde36, not in earlier commits)
defects.reproduction: With OMNI_API_TOKEN unset, authorizeMutation() on a request carrying 'X-Forwarded-For:' with an empty or whitespace-only value was ALLOWED. The header parsed to an empty chain, which was indistinguishable from 'no forwarding header present', so a remote client could send the header empty and be classified as local. Found by an independent adversarial probe written outside the repository's own test suite; the repository test had asserted only that malformed values 'must not crash', not that they must be denied.
defects.impact: A remote, unauthenticated attacker could bypass mutation authorization whenever OMNI_API_TOKEN was not configured, simply by sending an empty X-Forwarded-For header.
defects.fix: isTrustedLocalClient() now keys on the PRESENCE of a forwarding header rather than its parsed content. Any request carrying x-forwarded-for or x-real-ip is treated as proxied; with OMNI_TRUST_PROXY unset it is remote, and with the proxy trusted an unparseable nearest hop fails closed.
regressionTests: scripts/run_comprehensive_tests.js — adversarial suite tightened so every malformed/empty value must be DENIED (previously allowed-as-pass)
scripts/audit_safety.js — SAFE-17
defects.verification: PASS — 27-case independent probe (forged Origin/Referer, spoofed loopback, multi-hop, empty/whitespace/malformed headers, x-real-ip, trusted proxy, token paths, webhook paths): 27/27 as expected.

defects.title: Locality was inferred from the absence of a forwarding header, which the guard cannot actually verify
defects.introducedIn: design limitation present throughout the project (the guard only ever saw headers)
defects.reproduction: With OMNI_API_TOKEN unset, a request carrying NO forwarding header at all was treated as a direct local connection and allowed to mutate state. A remote client that connects directly (no proxy) sends exactly that, so it was indistinguishable from a desktop operator. Discovered by the new adversarial probe, which flagged 'no forwarding header at all' as allowed while the task required it to fail closed.
defects.impact: Any network client able to reach the port without going through a header-setting proxy could bypass mutation authorization whenever no token was configured.
defects.fix: Local trust must now be ASSERTED by the operator (OMNI_LOCAL_TRUST=true) or a token must be configured. Without either, every mutation and unauthenticated webhook call is denied 401 AUTH_NOT_CONFIGURED. The guard no longer pretends to detect locality it cannot observe.
regressionTests: scripts/adversarial_api_probe.js — 'header-less request denied when local trust is NOT asserted' and the full 48-case matrix
scripts/run_comprehensive_tests.js — 'API Guard: SEC-011 - with no token and no asserted local trust, mutations fail closed'
scripts/audit_safety.js — SAFE-09 (fail-closed without assertion; allowed with it)
defects.verification: PASS — production build 48/48; the deleted assertion also removes the misleading claim that header absence meant local.

defects.title: `git bundle verify` was treated as an integrity check, but it does not read the pack
defects.introducedIn: every recovery pass that reported bundles as verified
defects.reproduction: Truncated a valid bundle to 150 bytes. `git bundle verify` printed '<file> is okay', listed the ref and exited 0. `git clone` of the same file failed with 'fatal: early EOF / error: index-pack died'. The same held for a bundle with 400 bytes of junk written into its pack. Every prior report described bundles as 'verified' on the strength of that command.
defects.impact: A corrupted or truncated backup would have been declared sound, which is the worst possible failure mode for a recovery artefact — the team believes a backup exists and is restorable when it is neither.
defects.fix: audit_bundles.js now records two separate facts: `verify` = prerequisite check only (labelled 'pack NOT checked by this command') and `packIntegrity` = established solely by a successful clone plus fsck. The audit exits non-zero when a clone fails. The manifest and procedure state the limitation explicitly and give the four-part test for treating a bundle as sound. scripts/test_bundle_audit.js asserts that a truncated bundle still passes verify while failing restore, so the distinction cannot quietly disappear.
regressionTests: scripts/test_bundle_audit.js — 'a corrupted bundle fails the audit' (asserts verify says okay AND packIntegrity says unreadable)
scripts/audit_bundles.js — exit 1 when any restore fails
defects.verification: PASS — 21/21 negative tests; truncated bundle recorded as 'prerequisites ok' with 'pack NOT readable (clone failed)' and audit exit 1.

defects.title: Manifest claimed the in-repository bundle directory survived environment resets; the seventh reset destroyed it
defects.introducedIn: previous recovery pass, from a single observation that was generalised incorrectly
defects.reproduction: After the reset, `backups/` was absent (zero bundles) while untracked, not-ignored files such as CONFIGURATION.md, RECOVERY_MANIFEST.md, requirements.txt and scripts/audit_bundles.js were all present. Six bundles were destroyed.
defects.impact: The manifest told a future reader that the bundles were protected by their location. That was false, and it is exactly the assurance that must never be overstated: the difference between 'we have backups' and 'we have files that might be there'.
defects.fix: The generator now states the measured rule (the snapshot keeps files git does not ignore and drops ignored paths and anything outside the root), describes bundles as session-local, and gives the three commands to regenerate and re-audit them after a reset. DURABLE_BACKUP_NOT_ESTABLISHED is reaffirmed with no qualification.
regressionTests: RECOVERY_MANIFEST.md text is generated, so the claim cannot drift from the generator
scripts/verify_report_consistency.js requires the manifest's bundle rows to match backups/ on disk
defects.verification: PASS — manifest text now matches observed behaviour; consistency guard green with 1 bundle on disk.
defects.remainingDependency: Only an independently restored off-machine copy can change the durability status.

defects.title: Git-hygiene security test encoded a workspace snapshot and failed in every legitimate restore; its remote check also accepted look-alike repositories
defects.introducedIn: earlier passes (the same class of mistake as TEST-001: asserting the author's environment, not the security property)
defects.reproduction: Cloned the verified recovery bundle into a temporary directory, installed the pinned dependencies and ran pytest: 388 passed, 1 failed — 'master must remain a local branch'. A bundle restore, a single-branch clone or a CI checkout legitimately has only the checked-out branch locally, so the assertion failed for every consumer of the project while passing in the author's workspace. Writing the regression test for the fix then exposed a second bug: the remote check was a substring test, so 'https://github.com/veereshgowdan346-bot/Trade--fork.git' and a GitLab URL carrying the same owner path were both accepted.
defects.impact: The only failing check in a restored clone was a false positive, which trains people to ignore restore failures. Separately, the hygiene check that exists to catch a rogue remote would have waved through a look-alike fork.
defects.fix: master must now exist as a ref (local or origin/master) rather than as a convenience branch. Remote URLs are matched exactly on host and owner/repository, accepting only github.com paths equal to veereshgowdan346-bot/Trade- (plus the local .bundle path a verified restore creates). Added test_remote_url_predicate_rejects_unauthorised_destinations, which fails if the predicate is widened to accept a fork, a foreign host, file:// URLs or an empty value.
regressionTests: tests/test_phase71_security_closure_verification.py::test_git_branches_and_tags_hygiene
tests/test_phase71_security_closure_verification.py::test_remote_url_predicate_rejects_unauthorised_destinations
defects.verification: PASS — 390 passed in the workspace and 390 passed inside a clone of the verified bundle (previously 388/1 fail). The predicate test rejects all 7 unauthorised forms.

defects.title: A too-short OMNI_API_TOKEN was silently ignored, removing authentication entirely
defects.introducedIn: original guard design (token usability check `token.length >= 8` fell through)
defects.reproduction: With OMNI_LOCAL_TRUST=true and OMNI_API_TOKEN='abc123', a header-less request with no credentials was ALLOWED. The operator had configured a token and believed the API was authenticated; the guard treated the short value as absent and fell through to the token-less local path. Webhooks behaved the same way for a short configured secret.
defects.impact: A typo or a truncated .env value silently downgrades an authenticated deployment to unauthenticated. No warning is emitted, so the operator has no way to notice.
defects.fix: tokenState() distinguishes absent / usable / unusable. Present-but-unusable (blank or < 8 chars) now returns 401 AUTH_MISCONFIGURED on mutations and webhooks, and a configured-but-short webhook secret returns WEBHOOK_MISCONFIGURED. Empty is still treated as absent so a fresh .env works. Token precedence over OMNI_LOCAL_TRUST is explicit.
regressionTests: scripts/env_config_probe.js — token section (3 short values, precedence, empty=absent)
scripts/run_comprehensive_tests.js — 'API Guard: SEC-012 - a present but unusable token fails closed instead of being ignored'
scripts/mutation_check.js — SEC-012 mutant (MIN_TOKEN_LENGTH 8 -> 1) detected, 4 failing cases
defects.verification: PASS — production 43/43 env checks; mutant reproduced the old behaviour and is now detected.

defects.title: Vault status banner claimed credentials were 'encrypted with a development fallback key' after the fallback was removed
defects.introducedIn: SEC-003 removal left the UI copy behind
defects.reproduction: With VAULT_KEY unset, the UI displayed 'credentials are encrypted with a development fallback key'. In fact the vault fails closed and stores nothing; vaultUsingFallbackKey() now means 'unconfigured'.
defects.impact: False assurance: the operator is told encryption is happening (with a weak key) when the vault is actually disabled. Misleading security messaging is a defect in its own right.
defects.fix: Banner now states the vault is disabled and refuses to encrypt rather than using a fallback key. vault_key.ts documents that the legacy name means 'unconfigured'. SAFE-18 fails if the misleading text returns anywhere in src/.
regressionTests: scripts/audit_safety.js — SAFE-18 scans all src/**/*.ts(x) for the stale claim
defects.verification: PASS — SAFE-18 green; tsc and lint clean.
defects.remainingDependency: The API field name `fallbackKey` is retained for compatibility and documented as legacy.

defects.title: Adversarial suite did not exercise the SEC-008 path, so a reintroduced SEC-008 passed 44/44
defects.introducedIn: this pass (coverage gap in the new probe, found by mutation testing)
defects.reproduction: Mutation testing rebuilt apiGuard with 'originMatchesHost(req)' restored as an alternative to locality (mutant C). The probe reported 44 passed / 0 failed, because with OMNI_LOCAL_TRUST unset the function returns AUTH_NOT_CONFIGURED before ever reaching the origin check — the mutated line was unreachable in every case the probe covered.
defects.impact: A future regression of SEC-008 would have shipped green. The exact failure mode the SEC-010 incident demonstrated, repeated in a new test.
defects.fix: Added four cases that run with OMNI_LOCAL_TRUST asserted (the desktop deployment shape) and a remote client forging Origin / Referer / X-Forwarded-Host / loopback Host. Mutant C now fails 4 cases.
regressionTests: scripts/adversarial_api_probe.js — 'forged Origin+Host under asserted local trust' and three sibling cases
defects.verification: PASS — mutant C (SEC-008 reintroduced) detected: 44 passed / 4 failed; production 48/48.

defects.title: Rate limiter is per-process and keyed by a claimed IP
defects.reproduction: checkRateLimit() buckets on clientIp(); a caller rotating the claimed IP obtains fresh buckets.
defects.impact: Rate limiting is abuse control, not a security boundary; a determined caller can evade per-client limits.
defects.fix: Kept as-is. The server is a single-process Next.js desktop backend with no shared store, so a distributed limiter would add a dependency without a supported topology. Documented as best-effort abuse control; multi-instance or horizontally scaled deployment remains BLOCKED until a shared limiter exists.
regressionTests: scripts/run_comprehensive_tests.js — 'API Guard: rate limiter admits within limit and returns 429 beyond'
defects.verification: DOCUMENTED — limitation stated in the module docstring and in the release-readiness report.

defects.title: TypeScript vault fell back to a published constant passphrase
defects.reproduction: Previously masterKey() returned scrypt(constant) when VAULT_KEY was unset, so any vault created without a key was decryptable by anyone reading the repository.
defects.impact: Credential disclosure from any installation that had never set VAULT_KEY.
defects.fix: Derivation isolated in vault_key.ts; throws VaultKeyMissingError on missing/short keys; the route returns 503; no constant remains in the tree.
regressionTests: scripts/audit_safety.js — SAFE-14
defects.verification: PASS — re-probed this pass: missing key throws, short key rejected, valid key derives 32 bytes.

defects.title: Python credential manager fell back to a published constant password
defects.reproduction: The manager defaulted to a hardcoded master password when none was supplied.
defects.impact: Any vault written by the Python side was decryptable with a published constant.
defects.fix: Per-installation random master key written with os.open(..., 0o600); missing master password raises instead of falling back.
regressionTests: scripts/audit_safety.js — SAFE-13
defects.verification: PASS — re-probed this pass: 64-hex per-install key, mode 0600, no constant in source.

defects.title: Generated reports cited commit hashes that do not exist and asserted they were present
defects.introducedIn: generator templates carried hashes from earlier sandbox sessions
defects.reproduction: APEX_V2_FINAL_AUDIT_REPORT.md stated 'Baseline commit: 1ccee80...' and 'Baseline present | yes (1ccee80...)', but `git cat-file -t 1ccee80` reports the object does not exist locally or on origin. A 'Parent of baseline' row cited d095fc0..., also absent, and the certification report listed d095fc0/1ccee80 as places the historical material is 'retrievable from'. Verified with git cat-file -t for 60d7c41 (present), d095fc0, 1ccee80, 2af7e41, adba1be (all MISSING).
defects.impact: Reports asserted the existence of commits that are not in the repository, which is exactly the class of unverifiable evidence the project forbids. It also made a self-check ('baseline present: yes') that was never actually performed.
defects.fix: Baseline and parent are now read from git at generation time and existence is tested with `git cat-file -e`. The false 'retrievable from d095fc0/1ccee80' sentence was replaced with the one commit verified to exist (60d7c41). Absent earlier-session hashes are now explicitly labelled as not present. verify_report_consistency.js additionally requires the cited baseline to exist and to be an ancestor of HEAD.
regressionTests: scripts/verify_report_consistency.js — audit:baseline row, existence via git cat-file, ancestry via git merge-base
defects.verification: PASS — 82 claims, 0 failures; baseline now f61024e (verified present and reachable).
defects.remainingDependency: The 36 historical findings remain reachable from origin/master independent of this fix.

defects.title: Restored clones failed report consistency because the manifest describes a bundle inventory the clone does not contain
defects.introducedIn: the inventory guard added during this audit
defects.reproduction: Cloned any bundle and ran `node scripts/verify_report_consistency.js` inside it: it exited 1 with 'no bundles on disk — an empty inventory cannot be reported as a pass'. The clone was correct; it simply has no backups/ directory, because bundles are not committed.
defects.impact: Every restored snapshot would have shown a consistency failure, which is the check a future reader uses to decide whether the reports can be trusted. A check that always fails in the restore path trains people to ignore it, and could mask a real mismatch.
defects.fix: An absent backups/ directory is now reported as a note ('not applicable — this looks like a restored clone') and is not counted as a pass. Where the directory exists, every rule still applies. The audit tool keeps its own hard rule that an empty inventory is an error.
regressionTests: scripts/test_bundle_audit.js — 'archived names sit outside the live inventory, while a real gap still fails'
bundles 034025 and 034655 restore and verify clean inside their clones; 032901 and 033418 predate this fix and still show the old mismatch, which is why this record exists
defects.verification: PASS on bundles created after commit 69ebd04 (consistency REPORT_MATCHES_ARTIFACTS inside the clone, with the note). Earlier bundles keep their measured failure and are not relabelled.

defects.title: A bundle created from a shallow clone is unclonable, so a shallow workspace cannot produce a recovery artefact
defects.introducedIn: recovery after the eighth reset — the repository came back as a 1-commit shallow clone
defects.reproduction: After the eighth reset the workspace was shallow (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` = true). A bundle created with `git bundle create --all` from it produced `error: Could not read <sha>`, `fatal: Failed to traverse parents of commit df52c083`, `fatal: remote did not send all necessary objects`. `git bundle verify` on the same file still exited 0. After `git fetch --unshallow`, the identical command produced a bundle that clones cleanly (9 commits, fsck exit 0).
defects.impact: Every recovery artefact produced from a shallow workspace would have looked valid to `git bundle verify` and been unusable in a real restore — the same class of false assurance as REC-001, reached by a different route.
defects.fix: audit_bundles.js records `workspaceShallow` in every artefact and prints an explicit warning naming `git fetch --unshallow` when the source is shallow. The clone check already fails such a bundle, and scripts/test_bundle_audit.js now builds a bundle from a depth-1 clone and asserts the audit rejects it (exit 1, packIntegrity not readable). The recovered workspace was unshallowed before any further claim was made.
regressionTests: scripts/test_bundle_audit.js — 'a bundle whose source was shallow fails the clone check even though verify succeeds'
defects.verification: PASS — 26/26 negative tests; the shallow-source bundle is rejected by the audit although verify exits 0.
